source.text: Ἀλήθειαν λέγω ἐν Χριστῷ, οὐ ψεύδομαι, συμμαρτυρούσης μοι τῆς συνειδήσεώς μου ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ, ὅτι λύπη μοί ἐστιν μεγάλη καὶ ἀδιάλειπτος ὀδύνη τῇ καρδίᾳ μου·

records.literal_gloss: Truth I speak in Christ, not I lie, bearing witness with me the conscience of me in [the] Spirit Holy, \v 2 that grief to me is great and unceasing anguish in the heart of me;

en.L: I speak [the] truth in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, I am not lying, my conscience bearing witness with me in [the] Holy Spirit, \v 2 that I have great grief and unceasing anguish in my heart.
en.B: I am telling the truth in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}; I am not lying. My conscience, in the Holy Spirit, bears witness with me \v 2 that my sorrow is great and the pain in my heart never stops.
en.R: I belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and I am telling you the truth. I am not lying. My conscience agrees with what I say, and the Holy Spirit guides my conscience. \v 2 I am very sad, and my heart hurts all the time.

es.L: Digo [la] verdad en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, no miento, y mi conciencia da testimonio conmigo en [el] Espíritu Santo, \v 2 de que tengo una gran tristeza y un dolor incesante en mi corazón.
es.B: Estoy diciendo la verdad en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}; no miento. Mi conciencia, en el Espíritu Santo, me sirve de testigo \v 2 de que mi tristeza es grande y el dolor de mi corazón no cesa.
es.R: Pertenezco {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, y {{plural_you:les|os}} digo la verdad. No estoy mintiendo. Mi conciencia está de acuerdo con lo que digo, y el Espíritu Santo guía mi conciencia. \v 2 Estoy muy triste, y me duele el corazón todo el tiempo.

sw.L: Kweli ninaisema katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, sidanganyi, dhamiri yangu ikitoa ushahidi pamoja nami katika Roho Mtakatifu, \v 2 kwamba huzuni yangu ni kubwa na uchungu usiokoma umo moyoni mwangu.
sw.B: Ninasema kweli katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}; sidanganyi. Dhamiri yangu, katika Roho Mtakatifu, inashuhudia pamoja nami \v 2 kwamba nina huzuni kubwa, na maumivu ya moyo wangu hayakomi.
sw.R: Mimi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, na ninawaambia kweli. Sidanganyi. Dhamiri yangu inakubaliana na ninachosema, na Roho Mtakatifu anaiongoza dhamiri yangu. \v 2 Nina huzuni sana, na moyo wangu unauma wakati wote.

decisions.choice: in Christ: speaking as one who belongs to Christ
decisions.reason: Paul speaks as a man joined to Christ and answerable to him, so his words can be trusted. He says the same in 2 Corinthians 2:17 and 12:19.

decisions.choice: his conscience is a second witness, and the Holy Spirit stands behind it
alternatives: "in the Holy Spirit" goes with "I speak"
decisions.reason: The participle συμμαρτυρούσης means "bearing witness together with". Paul's own word and his conscience make two witnesses (compare Deuteronomy 19:15). "In the Holy Spirit" most likely goes with the conscience: the Spirit confirms what it says, as in 8:16.

decisions.choice: the cause of his grief is left unsaid until verse 3
decisions.reason: Paul states his grief before he names its cause: most of his own people, Israel, have not believed in the Messiah (verses 3-5, 30-32; 10:1).

decisions.choice: I belong to Christ; the Holy Spirit guides my conscience
decisions.reason: Readable turns "in Christ" and "in the Holy Spirit" into short sentences, as the meaning decisions explain them.

source.text: ηὐχόμην γὰρ ἀνάθεμα εἶναι αὐτὸς ἐγὼ ἀπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν συγγενῶν μου κατὰ σάρκα, οἵτινές εἰσιν Ἰσραηλῖται, ὧν ἡ υἱοθεσία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ αἱ διαθῆκαι καὶ ἡ νομοθεσία καὶ ἡ λατρεία καὶ αἱ ἐπαγγελίαι, ὧν οἱ πατέρες, καὶ ἐξ ὧν ὁ χριστὸς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα, ὁ ὢν ἐπὶ πάντων, θεὸς εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.

records.literal_gloss: For was wishing accursed to be myself I from the Christ on behalf of the brothers of me, the kinsmen of me according to flesh, \v 4 who are Israelites, of whom the adoption and the glory and the covenants and the lawgiving and the worship and the promises, \v 5 of whom the fathers, and from whom the Christ, the [part] according to flesh, the [one] being over all, God blessed to the ages; amen.

en.L: For I could wish that I myself were accursed [and cut off] from the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} for the sake of my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, my kinsfolk according to [the] flesh, \v 4 who are Israelites, to whom [belong] the adoption and the glory and the covenants and the giving of the law and the worship and the promises, \v 5 to whom [belong] the fathers, and from whom [is] the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} according to the flesh, who is over all, God blessed to the ages. Amen.
en.B: I could even wish that I myself were under a curse, cut off from {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, on behalf of my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, my own people by human descent. \v 4 They are Israelites. Theirs is the adoption as God's children, theirs the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the worship and the promises. \v 5 The patriarchs are theirs, and from them, by human descent, comes {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, who is God over all, blessed forever. Amen.
en.R: I would even be willing to be cursed and cut off from {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, if that could help my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, my own people by birth. \v 4 They are the people of Israel. God adopted them as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children and showed them {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory. He made covenants with them and gave them the law. He showed them how to worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promises. \v 5 Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were their ancestors. And as a human being, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} came from their people. He is God over all things, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is to be praised forever. Amen.

es.L: Porque yo mismo desearía ser maldito, [separado] {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, por amor a mis hermanos, mis parientes según [la] carne, \v 4 que son israelitas, de quienes [son] la adopción y la gloria y los pactos y la promulgación de la ley y el culto y las promesas, \v 5 de quienes [son] los padres, y de quienes [procede] {{christos:el Cristo|el Mesías}} según la carne, el cual es sobre todas las cosas, Dios bendito por los siglos. Amén.
es.B: Hasta desearía estar yo mismo bajo maldición, separado {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, por el bien de mis hermanos, los de mi propia sangre. \v 4 Son israelitas. A ellos pertenecen la adopción como hijos de Dios, la gloria, los pactos, la entrega de la ley, el culto y las promesas. \v 5 Suyos son los patriarcas, y de ellos, según su linaje humano, viene {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, que es Dios sobre todo, bendito para siempre. Amén.
es.R: Hasta estaría dispuesto a ser maldito y separado {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, si eso pudiera ayudar a mis hermanos, los de mi propio pueblo por nacimiento. \v 4 Son el pueblo de Israel. Dios los adoptó como {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hijos y les mostró {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria. Hizo pactos con ellos y les dio la ley. Les enseñó cómo debían adorar a Dios, y les dio {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} promesas. \v 5 Abraham, Isaac y Jacob fueron sus antepasados. Y como ser humano, {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} vino de su pueblo. Él es Dios sobre todas las cosas, y merece ser alabado para siempre. Amén.

sw.L: Kwa maana ningetamani mimi mwenyewe niwe nimelaaniwa [na kutengwa] mbali na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kwa ajili ya ndugu zangu, jamaa zangu kwa kadiri ya mwili, \v 4 ambao ni Waisraeli, ambao kwao [kuna] kufanywa kuwa wana, na utukufu, na maagano, na utoaji wa sheria, na ibada, na ahadi, \v 5 ambao kwao [kuna] mababa, na kutoka kwao [ametoka] {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kwa kadiri ya mwili, aliye juu ya vyote, Mungu anayehimidiwa hata milele. Amina.
sw.B: Ningeweza hata kutamani mimi mwenyewe niwe chini ya laana na kutengwa na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kwa ajili ya ndugu zangu, watu wa taifa langu kwa ukoo wa kibinadamu. \v 4 Wao ni Waisraeli. Ni wao waliofanywa kuwa wana wa Mungu; ni wao wenye utukufu, maagano, sheria waliyopewa, ibada na ahadi. \v 5 Mababu wa taifa ni wao, na kutoka kwao, kwa ukoo wa kibinadamu, ametoka {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, aliye Mungu juu ya vyote, anayehimidiwa milele. Amina.
sw.R: Ningekuwa tayari hata kulaaniwa na kutengwa na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kama hilo lingewasaidia ndugu zangu, watu wa taifa langu kwa kuzaliwa. \v 4 Wao ni watu wa Israeli. Mungu aliwafanya kuwa wana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na kuwaonyesha utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Alifanya maagano nao na kuwapa sheria. Aliwaonyesha jinsi ya kumwabudu, na akawapa ahadi {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. \v 5 Ibrahimu, Isaka na Yakobo walikuwa mababu zao. Na kama mwanadamu, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alitoka katika taifa lao. Yeye ni Mungu juu ya vitu vyote, na anastahili kusifiwa milele. Amina.

decisions.choice: accursed: handed over to God's judgment and cut off from Christ
decisions.reason: ἀνάθεμα is something devoted to God for destruction (Joshua 6:17, 7:1), and so a person under God's curse (1 Corinthians 16:22, Galatians 1:8-9). "From Christ" says what the curse would mean for Paul: being cut off from him.

decisions.choice: a wish he cannot carry out
decisions.reason: The imperfect ηὐχόμην expresses a wish that cannot or will not come true: "I could wish". Paul echoes Moses, who asked to be blotted out of God's book if Israel could not be forgiven (Exodus 32:32). Romans 8:38-39 has just said nothing can separate him from Christ.

decisions.choice: according to the flesh: by physical descent
decisions.reason: σάρξ here is human birth and family line, not the sinful self: the Jews are Paul's people by birth, and the Messiah is from Israel as a human being, as in 1:3.

decisions.choice: the adoption: Israel made God's son
decisions.reason: God called Israel "my firstborn son" (Exodus 4:22; Hosea 11:1). Paul has used the same word for believers in 8:15 and 8:23.

decisions.choice: the glory: God's glorious presence among Israel
decisions.reason: The glory is God's presence shown to Israel at Sinai, in the tabernacle and in the temple (Exodus 24:16-17, 40:34; 1 Kings 8:10-11).

decisions.choice: the worship: the worship God gave Israel in the tabernacle and temple
decisions.reason: λατρεία is service offered to God, here the priesthood, sacrifices and festivals of the law (Hebrews 9:1, 9:6). Paul uses it for the worship of believers in 12:1.

decisions.choice: Christ "who is God over all, blessed forever": the words describe the Messiah
alternatives: a full stop after "according to the flesh": "May God, who is over all, be blessed forever"
a stop after "over all": "the Messiah, who is over all. God be blessed forever"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates with a comma after "according to the flesh", so that "who is over all, God blessed forever" describes the Messiah. In favor: the words "who is" most naturally refer back to the person just named; "according to the flesh" leads one to expect what he is beyond his human descent; and a separate blessing of God normally puts "blessed" first ("Blessed be God", 2 Corinthians 1:3), while here it follows the one just named, as in 1:25 and 2 Corinthians 11:31. Against: Paul nowhere else plainly calls Christ "God", and some manuscripts and readers put a full stop after "flesh", making the rest a separate praise: "God who is over all be blessed forever." The oldest manuscripts have no punctuation, so the choice is made from the sense.

decisions.choice: by human descent (B); by birth, as a human being (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "according to the flesh" means here, as Romans 1:3 does.

decisions.choice: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: Readable names "the fathers": the patriarchs with whom God made his promises (Exodus 3:15).

decisions.choice: God adopted them; showed them his glory; made covenants; gave them the law; showed them how to worship
decisions.reason: Readable turns the list of nouns into sentences that say what God did for Israel, following the meaning decisions.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As at 1:13, Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so there is no gender span.

decisions.choice: maldito (L, R); bajo maldición (B)
decisions.reason: Spanish has the Greek word as "anatema", but to most readers it now means excommunication by a church. "Maldito" and "bajo maldición" say what the meaning decision says: handed over to God's judgment.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: As at 1:13, "ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili needs no gender span here.

source.text: Οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι ἐκπέπτωκεν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Not such however as that has fallen the word of the God.

en.L: But [it is] not as though the word of God has failed.
en.B: But this does not mean that God's word has failed.
en.R: But this does not mean that God has failed to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promises.

es.L: Pero no [es] como si la palabra de Dios hubiera fallado.
es.B: Pero esto no quiere decir que la palabra de Dios haya fracasado.
es.R: Pero esto no significa que Dios no haya cumplido {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} promesas.

sw.L: Lakini [hii] si kusema kwamba neno la Mungu limeanguka.
sw.B: Lakini hii haimaanishi kwamba neno la Mungu limeshindwa.
sw.R: Lakini hii haimaanishi kwamba Mungu ameshindwa kutimiza ahadi {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.

decisions.choice: the word of God: God's promises to Israel
decisions.reason: Paul has just listed the promises (verse 4), and verse 9 calls God's word to Abraham "a word of promise". The question is whether Israel's unbelief means those promises have come to nothing.

decisions.choice: has failed: has fallen short of its purpose
decisions.reason: ἐκπίπτω is to fall, and so to fail or come to nothing (compare 1 Corinthians 13:8).

decisions.choice: failed to keep his promises
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the word of God" refers to here.

source.text: οὐ γὰρ πάντες οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραήλ, οὗτοι Ἰσραήλ·

records.literal_gloss: Not for all the [ones] from Israel, these [are] Israel;

en.L: For not all who [are] from Israel, these [are] Israel;
en.B: For not everyone descended from Israel truly belongs to Israel.
en.R: Not everyone who is born into the family of Israel is part of the true Israel, God's people.

es.L: Porque no todos los que [son] de Israel, estos [son] Israel;
es.B: Porque no todos los que descienden de Israel pertenecen de verdad a Israel.
es.R: No todos los que nacen en la familia de Israel forman parte del verdadero Israel, el pueblo de Dios.

sw.L: Kwa maana si wote walio wa Israeli, hao ndio Israeli;
sw.B: Kwa maana si kila aliyetoka katika ukoo wa Israeli ni wa Israeli kweli.
sw.R: Si kila mtu aliyezaliwa katika jamaa ya Israeli ni sehemu ya Israeli halisi, yaani watu wa Mungu.

decisions.choice: two senses of Israel: the people descended from Jacob, and the people of God's promise within it
alternatives: the second "Israel" is the church of Jews and Gentiles
decisions.reason: The first "Israel" is the nation by descent from Jacob, whose other name was Israel (Genesis 32:28). The second is the people God has chosen and called, who are not simply the same as the nation (verses 7-13; compare 2:28-29 and 11:5). Here Paul is still speaking of Israel; he is not calling Gentile believers "Israel".

decisions.choice: truly belongs to (B); the true Israel, God's people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the repeated "Israel" means, following the meaning decision.

source.text: οὐδ’ ὅτι εἰσὶν σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ, πάντες τέκνα, ἀλλ’· Ἐν Ἰσαὰκ κληθήσεταί σοι σπέρμα.

records.literal_gloss: Nor because they are seed of Abraham [are they] all children, but: In Isaac will be called to you seed.

en.L: Nor, because they are Abraham's seed, [are they] all [his] children, but: "Through Isaac your seed will be named."
en.B: Nor are they all Abraham's children just because they are his descendants. Rather, "It is through Isaac that your offspring will be named."
en.R: And not all of Abraham's descendants are truly his children. God told Abraham, "Your family line will be counted through Isaac."

es.L: Ni, porque son descendencia de Abraham, [son] todos [sus] hijos, sino: «Por Isaac será llamada tu descendencia».
es.B: Ni tampoco son todos hijos de Abraham por el solo hecho de ser sus descendientes. Al contrario: «Por medio de Isaac se nombrará tu descendencia».
es.R: Y no todos los descendientes de Abraham son de verdad sus hijos. Dios le dijo a Abraham: «Tu descendencia se contará por medio de Isaac».

sw.L: Wala, kwa kuwa ni uzao wa Ibrahimu, si wote [ni] watoto [wake], bali: "Kupitia Isaka uzao wako utatajwa."
sw.B: Wala si wote ni watoto wa Ibrahimu kwa sababu tu ni wazawa wake. Badala yake, "Uzao wako utatajwa kupitia Isaka."
sw.R: Na si wazao wote wa Ibrahimu ni watoto wake kweli. Mungu alimwambia Ibrahimu, "Ukoo wako utahesabiwa kupitia Isaka."

decisions.choice: Genesis 21:12
decisions.reason: God says this to Abraham when Sarah wants Hagar and Ishmael sent away: Abraham's promised line will come through Isaac, not through Ishmael, though both were his sons. Paul quotes the Greek Old Testament word for word.

decisions.choice: will be named: will be reckoned as your offspring
decisions.reason: καλέω is "call" or "name". In Genesis it means that Isaac's line will count as Abraham's offspring. Paul goes on to use the same verb for God's calling (verses 12, 24-26).

decisions.choice: God told Abraham
decisions.reason: Readable says who spoke the words of the quotation and to whom (Genesis 21:12).

decisions.choice: descendencia
decisions.reason: "Simiente" is the word of older Spanish Bibles and now sounds agricultural. "Descendencia" is the everyday word and, like the Greek, is a collective singular, so it can mean one heir or a whole people; verses 8 and 29 use it too.

source.text: τοῦτ’ ἔστιν, οὐ τὰ τέκνα τῆς σαρκὸς ταῦτα τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀλλὰ τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐπαγγελίας λογίζεται εἰς σπέρμα·

records.literal_gloss: That is, not the children of the flesh, these [are] children of the God, but the children of the promise are counted for seed;

en.L: That is, [it is] not the children of the flesh [who are] children of God, but the children of the promise are counted as seed.
en.B: This means that it is not the children born by natural descent who are God's children. It is the children of the promise who are counted as Abraham's offspring.
en.R: This means that being born into Abraham's family does not make anyone a child of God. The children born because of God's promise are the ones counted as Abraham's true family.

es.L: Esto es, no los hijos de la carne [son] hijos de Dios, sino que los hijos de la promesa son contados como descendencia.
es.B: Esto significa que no son los hijos nacidos por descendencia natural los que son hijos de Dios, sino que son los hijos de la promesa los que se cuentan como descendencia de Abraham.
es.R: Esto quiere decir que nacer en la familia de Abraham no hace a nadie hijo de Dios. Los hijos que nacieron por la promesa de Dios son los que cuentan como la verdadera familia de Abraham.

sw.L: Hii ni kusema, watoto wa mwili, hao si watoto wa Mungu, bali watoto wa ahadi ndio wanaohesabiwa kuwa uzao.
sw.B: Maana yake ni kwamba si watoto waliozaliwa kwa njia ya kawaida ya kibinadamu walio watoto wa Mungu. Ni watoto wa ahadi wanaohesabiwa kuwa uzao wa Ibrahimu.
sw.R: Hii inamaanisha kwamba kuzaliwa katika jamaa ya Ibrahimu hakumfanyi mtu yeyote kuwa mtoto wa Mungu. Watoto waliozaliwa kwa sababu ya ahadi ya Mungu ndio wanaohesabiwa kuwa jamaa halisi ya Ibrahimu.

decisions.choice: children of the flesh: children by natural birth only
decisions.reason: σάρξ here is ordinary human descent, as with Ishmael, who was "born according to the flesh" (Galatians 4:23), in contrast to Isaac, born by God's promise.

decisions.choice: children of the promise: those born because of what God promised
decisions.reason: Isaac was born because God promised him to Abraham and Sarah when they were too old to have children (4:18-21, Genesis 18:10-14). Paul makes him the pattern for all whom God counts as Abraham's offspring (Galatians 4:28).

decisions.choice: are counted: are reckoned by God
decisions.reason: λογίζομαι is the verb Paul used in chapter 4 for faith being counted as righteousness (4:3-5). God himself decides who are counted as Abraham's offspring.

decisions.choice: Abraham's offspring (B); Abraham's true family (R)
decisions.reason: The offspring are Abraham's, as in verse 7; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: by natural descent
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "of the flesh" means here; it is not the sinful self of 8:3-9.

source.text: ἐπαγγελίας γὰρ ὁ λόγος οὗτος· Κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦτον ἐλεύσομαι καὶ ἔσται τῇ Σάρρᾳ υἱός.

records.literal_gloss: Of promise for the word this [is]: At the time this I will come and there will be to the Sarah a son.

en.L: For this word [is a word] of promise: "At this time I will come, and Sarah will have a son."
en.B: For this is what the promise said: "At this time I will come back, and a son will be born to Sarah."
en.R: This is the promise God made: "At this time next year I will come back, and Sarah will have a son."

es.L: Porque esta palabra [es una palabra] de promesa: «Por este tiempo vendré, y Sara tendrá un hijo».
es.B: Porque esto es lo que dijo la promesa: «Por este tiempo volveré, y a Sara le nacerá un hijo».
es.R: Esta es la promesa que hizo Dios: «Por este tiempo, el año que viene, volveré, y Sara tendrá un hijo».

sw.L: Kwa maana neno hili [ni neno] la ahadi: "Wakati huu nitakuja, na Sara atakuwa na mwana."
sw.B: Kwa maana hivi ndivyo ahadi ilivyosema: "Wakati kama huu nitarudi, na Sara atazaa mwana."
sw.R: Hii ndiyo ahadi ambayo Mungu alitoa: "Mwaka ujao wakati kama huu nitarudi, na Sara atakuwa na mtoto wa kiume."

decisions.choice: Genesis 18:10 and 18:14
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham at Mamre that Sarah, old and without children, would have a son "at the set time", that is, about a year later. Paul combines the wording of the two verses in their Greek form. In the Hebrew of 18:14 the speaker is named with the divine name.

decisions.choice: the emphasis falls on "promise"
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "of promise" first: this word was a promise, so Isaac was a child of the promise (verse 8), not merely of natural birth.

decisions.choice: At this time next year
decisions.reason: In Genesis 18:10 and 18:14 "this time" means the same season a year later; Readable says so.

source.text: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ Ῥεβέκκα ἐξ ἑνὸς κοίτην ἔχουσα, Ἰσαὰκ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Not only and, but also Rebecca, from one conception having, Isaac the father of us;

en.L: And not only [that], but also Rebecca, having conceived by one [man], Isaac our father;
en.B: And that is not all. Rebecca also conceived children by one man, our forefather Isaac.
en.R: Here is another example. Rebecca became pregnant with twins, and both had the same father, our ancestor Isaac.

es.L: Y no solo [esto], sino también Rebeca, habiendo concebido de uno [solo], de Isaac nuestro padre;
es.B: Y no solo eso. También Rebeca concibió hijos de un solo hombre, nuestro antepasado Isaac.
es.R: Hay otro ejemplo. Rebeca quedó embarazada de gemelos, y los dos tenían el mismo padre, nuestro antepasado Isaac.

sw.L: Na si hilo peke yake, bali pia Rebeka, aliyepata mimba kwa [mwanamume] mmoja, Isaka baba yetu;
sw.B: Na hilo silo pekee. Rebeka pia alipata mimba ya watoto kwa mwanamume mmoja, babu yetu Isaka.
sw.R: Kuna mfano mwingine. Rebeka alipata mimba ya mapacha, na wote wawili walikuwa na baba mmoja, babu yetu Isaka.

decisions.choice: an unfinished sentence, taken up again in verses 11-12
decisions.reason: The Greek has no main verb: Paul begins with Rebecca, breaks off to explain (verse 11), and finishes with "it was said to her" (verse 12). A verb such as "conceived" or "had children" is understood.

decisions.choice: conceived by one man: both sons had the same father and the same conception
decisions.reason: κοίτη means a bed, and so conception. The point is that Jacob and Esau were twins, with the same father and mother (Genesis 25:21-24), unlike Ishmael and Isaac. Descent made no difference between them.

decisions.choice: our father Isaac: ancestor of Israel, and of all who believe
decisions.reason: Isaac is "our father" because Paul is a Jew; he has also called Abraham the father of all who believe (4:11-12, 4:16).

decisions.choice: pregnant with twins
decisions.reason: Readable says what "conceived by one man" points to, from Genesis 25:24.

source.text: μήπω γὰρ γεννηθέντων μηδὲ πραξάντων τι ἀγαθὸν ἢ φαῦλον, ἵνα ἡ κατ’ ἐκλογὴν πρόθεσις τοῦ θεοῦ μένῃ, οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἀλλ’ ἐκ τοῦ καλοῦντος, ἐρρέθη αὐτῇ ὅτι Ὁ μείζων δουλεύσει τῷ ἐλάσσονι·

records.literal_gloss: For not yet having been born nor having done anything good or bad, so that the according to election purpose of the God might remain, \v 12 not from works but from the [one] calling, it was said to her that: The greater will serve the lesser;

en.L: For [when they had] not yet been born nor done anything good or bad, so that the purpose of God according to election might stand, \v 12 not from works but from the [one] who calls, it was said to her, "The older will serve the younger."
en.B: The children were not yet born and had done nothing good or bad. Yet so that God's purpose in choosing might stand, \v 12 a purpose that rests not on works but on the one who calls, Rebecca was told, "The older will serve the younger."
en.R: Her sons had not yet been born. They had not done anything good or bad. God made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} choice then, so that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} plan would stand firm. \v 12 It depends on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} call, not on what people do. So God told Rebecca, "The older son will serve the younger one."

es.L: Porque [cuando] aún no habían nacido ni habían hecho nada bueno o malo, para que el propósito de Dios conforme a [la] elección permaneciera, \v 12 no por [las] obras sino por el que llama, se le dijo a ella: «El mayor servirá al menor».
es.B: Los niños aún no habían nacido ni habían hecho nada bueno ni malo. Pero, para que se mantuviera firme el propósito de Dios al elegir, \v 12 un propósito que no se basa en las obras sino en aquel que llama, a Rebeca se le dijo: «El mayor servirá al menor».
es.R: Sus hijos todavía no habían nacido. No habían hecho nada bueno ni malo. Ya entonces Dios hizo {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} elección, para que {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} plan se mantuviera firme. \v 12 Ese plan depende de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} llamado, no de lo que hace la gente. Por eso Dios le dijo a Rebeca: «El hijo mayor servirá al menor».

sw.L: Kwa maana [walipokuwa] bado hawajazaliwa wala hawajatenda jambo lolote jema au baya, ili kusudi la Mungu kwa kadiri ya uchaguzi lipate kudumu, \v 12 si kutokana na matendo bali kutokana na yule aitaye, aliambiwa kwamba: "Aliye mkubwa atamtumikia aliye mdogo."
sw.B: Watoto walikuwa bado hawajazaliwa, na hawakuwa wamefanya lolote jema au baya. Hata hivyo, ili kusudi la Mungu katika kuchagua lisimame imara, \v 12 kusudi lisilotegemea matendo bali yule anayeita, Rebeka aliambiwa, "Mkubwa atamtumikia mdogo wake."
sw.R: Wana wake walikuwa bado hawajazaliwa. Hawakuwa wamefanya lolote jema wala baya. Mungu alifanya uchaguzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakati huo, ili mpango {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} usimame imara. \v 12 Mpango huo unategemea wito {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, si yale wanayofanya watu. Kwa hiyo Mungu alimwambia Rebeka, "Mwana mkubwa atamtumikia mdogo wake."

decisions.choice: Genesis 25:23
decisions.reason: God told Rebecca, while the twins struggled within her, that two nations were in her womb and that the older would serve the younger. Paul quotes the last line of the oracle as it stands in the Greek Old Testament.

decisions.choice: God's purpose according to election: his plan, carried out by his choosing
alternatives: God's purpose of foreseeing who would choose him
decisions.reason: ἐκλογή is choosing or election, and πρόθεσις is purpose or plan (8:28). God's plan works by his own choice, and it "stands", that is, it holds and is carried out.

decisions.choice: the choice rests on God who calls, not on anything done
decisions.reason: Paul stresses that God spoke before the twins were born or had done good or bad. The choice did not depend on works but on God, "the one who calls" (as in 4:17, 8:30).

decisions.choice: the greater, the lesser: the older and the younger
decisions.reason: In Genesis 25:23 the words mean the elder and the younger son, Esau and Jacob.

decisions.choice: what people do
decisions.reason: Readable says "what people do" for "works", as the Romans drafts do throughout.

decisions.choice: Rebecca
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the woman "her" refers to (verse 10).

decisions.choice: God made his choice then
decisions.reason: Readable makes the election in "purpose according to election" a sentence of its own.

source.text: καθὼς γέγραπται· Τὸν Ἰακὼβ ἠγάπησα, τὸν δὲ Ἠσαῦ ἐμίσησα.

records.literal_gloss: Just as it has been written: The Jacob I loved, but the Esau I hated.

en.L: Just as it is written, "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated."
en.B: As it is written, "I loved Jacob, but Esau I hated."
en.R: As Scripture says, "I chose to love Jacob, but I rejected Esau."

es.L: Así como está escrito: «A Jacob amé, pero a Esaú aborrecí».
es.B: Como está escrito: «Amé a Jacob, pero a Esaú lo odié».
es.R: Como dice la Escritura: «Escogí amar a Jacob, pero rechacé a Esaú».

sw.L: Kama ilivyoandikwa: "Yakobo nilimpenda, lakini Esau nilimchukia."
sw.B: Kama ilivyoandikwa, "Nilimpenda Yakobo, lakini Esau nilimchukia."
sw.R: Kama Maandiko yasemavyo, "Nilichagua kumpenda Yakobo, lakini nilimkataa Esau."

decisions.choice: Malachi 1:2-3
decisions.reason: Through Malachi, centuries after Jacob and Esau, God answers Israel's doubt of his love by pointing to what happened to their brother nation Edom, descended from Esau (Malachi 1:2-5). In the Hebrew the speaker is named with the divine name. Paul quotes the Greek Old Testament with the names moved to the front.

decisions.choice: loved and hated: chose and did not choose
alternatives: God's feelings of love and hatred toward each
God's active judgment on Esau and Edom
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew way of speaking, "love" and "hate" side by side often mean choosing one and setting the other aside, not feelings: Jacob "loved Rachel more than Leah" and Leah is said to be "hated" (Genesis 29:30-31); compare Luke 14:26 with Matthew 10:37. Here God chose Jacob's line for his covenant and not Esau's. Some take "hated" more strongly, as God's judgment on Edom, which Malachi 1:3-4 goes on to describe.

decisions.choice: the brothers and the peoples descended from them
decisions.reason: Genesis 25:23 and Malachi 1:2-5 speak of the two brothers as the heads of two nations, Israel and Edom. Paul's point is that God's choosing did not depend on birth or works. Whether he is thinking of the choice of individuals for salvation or of the roles of peoples in God's plan is debated; the passage may hold both.

decisions.choice: I chose to love; I rejected
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom as the meaning decision describes it, since "hated" alone suggests a feeling the words do not mean. Literal and Balanced keep "loved" and "hated".

source.text: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν;

records.literal_gloss: What then will we say?

en.L: What then will we say?
en.B: What then are we to say?
en.R: So what should we say about this?

es.L: ¿Qué, pues, diremos?
es.B: ¿Qué diremos entonces?
es.R: Entonces, ¿qué debemos decir de esto?

sw.L: Basi tutasema nini?
sw.B: Basi, tuseme nini?
sw.R: Basi, tunapaswa kusema nini kuhusu jambo hili?

decisions.choice: Paul raises an objection to answer it
decisions.reason: Paul uses this question to bring up a conclusion someone might draw from what he has said (as in 3:5, 4:1, 6:1, 7:7, 8:31).

source.text: μὴ ἀδικία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ;

records.literal_gloss: Not injustice with the God?

en.L: Is there injustice with God?
en.B: Is there injustice on God's part?
en.R: Is God unfair?

es.L: ¿Acaso [hay] injusticia en Dios?
es.B: ¿Hay injusticia de parte de Dios?
es.R: ¿Es Dios injusto?

sw.L: Je, kwa Mungu kuna kutokuwa na haki?
sw.B: Je, Mungu anatenda udhalimu?
sw.R: Je, Mungu hatendi haki?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: The question begins with μὴ, which expects a negative answer: "Surely there is no injustice with God?"

decisions.choice: injustice: wrongdoing, failing to be right
decisions.reason: ἀδικία is the opposite of righteousness: if God chose Jacob before either did anything, is God acting unrighteously? Paul asked a similar question in 3:5.

decisions.choice: unfair
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for injustice in a choice between two people.

source.text: μὴ γένοιτο·

records.literal_gloss: Not may it be;

en.L: May it not be!
en.B: Certainly not!
en.R: Of course not!

es.L: ¡Que no sea así!
es.B: ¡De ninguna manera!
es.R: ¡Por supuesto que no!

sw.L: Isiwe hivyo!
sw.B: Hata kidogo!
sw.R: Hapana kabisa!

decisions.choice: the strongest possible denial
decisions.reason: μὴ γένοιτο, "may it not happen", is Paul's strongest way of rejecting a false conclusion (3:4, 3:6, 6:2, 11:1).

decisions.choice: Certainly not! (B); Of course not! (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use ordinary English for an emphatic no, as Galatians does. "God forbid" adds a word for God that the Greek does not have.

source.text: τῷ Μωϋσεῖ γὰρ λέγει· Ἐλεήσω ὃν ἂν ἐλεῶ, καὶ οἰκτιρήσω ὃν ἂν οἰκτίρω.

records.literal_gloss: To the Moses for he says: I will have mercy on whom ever I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom ever I have compassion.

en.L: For to Moses {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "I will have mercy on whomever I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whomever I have compassion."
en.B: For God says to Moses, "I will have mercy on whomever I have mercy, and I will show compassion to whomever I show compassion."
en.R: God said to Moses, "I will show mercy to anyone I choose. I will be kind to anyone I choose."

es.L: Porque a Moisés {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dice: «Tendré misericordia de quien tenga misericordia, y me compadeceré de quien me compadezca».
es.B: Porque Dios dice a Moisés: «Tendré misericordia de quien yo tenga misericordia, y mostraré compasión a quien yo muestre compasión».
es.R: Dios le dijo a Moisés: «Mostraré misericordia a quien yo elija. Seré bondadoso con quien yo elija».

sw.L: Kwa maana anamwambia Musa: "Nitamrehemu yule ambaye ninamrehemu, na nitamwonea huruma yule ambaye ninamwonea huruma."
sw.B: Kwa maana Mungu anamwambia Musa, "Nitamrehemu yeyote nitakayemrehemu, na nitamhurumia yeyote nitakayemhurumia."
sw.R: Mungu alimwambia Musa, "Nitamwonyesha rehema yeyote ninayemchagua. Nitamwonea huruma yeyote ninayemchagua."

decisions.choice: Exodus 33:19
decisions.reason: After Israel made the golden calf, Moses asked to see God's glory. God answered that he would pass by and proclaim his name, and added these words. Paul quotes the Greek Old Testament word for word. The words come just after God has spared Israel in mercy.

decisions.choice: "on whom I have mercy": God alone decides
decisions.reason: Repeating the verb ("I will have mercy on whom I have mercy") is a Hebrew way of saying that the decision is God's own and is not controlled by anything outside him (compare Exodus 3:14).

decisions.choice: the speaker is God
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject; the words are God's in Exodus 33:19.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

decisions.choice: anyone I choose; be kind
decisions.reason: Readable explains the repeated verb as the meaning decision describes it, and uses a simpler word for compassion.

decisions.choice: kurehemu, rehema (mercy); kuhurumia, kuonea huruma (compassion)
decisions.reason: Swahili often uses "huruma" for both ideas. Keeping "kurehemu" and "rehema" for the Greek mercy verb and "huruma" for the compassion verb keeps the two Greek verbs apart, and lets "rehema" carry the mercy of verses 16, 18 and 23.

source.text: ἄρα οὖν οὐ τοῦ θέλοντος οὐδὲ τοῦ τρέχοντος ἀλλὰ τοῦ ἐλεῶντος θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: So then not of the [one] willing nor of the [one] running but of the showing mercy God.

en.L: So then [it is] not of the [one] who wills nor of the [one] who runs, but of God who shows mercy.
en.B: So it is not a matter of what a person wants or how hard a person strives, but of God, who shows mercy.
en.R: So God's choice does not depend on what people want or on how hard they try. It depends on God, who shows mercy.

es.L: Así pues, no [es] del que quiere ni del que corre, sino del Dios que muestra misericordia.
es.B: Así que no depende de lo que alguien quiera ni de cuánto se esfuerce, sino de Dios, que muestra misericordia.
es.R: Así que la elección de Dios no depende de lo que la gente quiere ni de cuánto se esfuerza. Depende de Dios, que muestra misericordia.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo basi, [si jambo] la yule anayetaka wala la yule anayekimbia, bali la Mungu anayerehemu.
sw.B: Basi jambo hili halitegemei kile mtu anachotaka wala jinsi anavyojitahidi, bali linamtegemea Mungu, anayerehemu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo uchaguzi wa Mungu hautegemei kile watu wanachotaka wala jinsi wanavyojitahidi. Unamtegemea Mungu, anayeonyesha rehema.

decisions.choice: "it" is God's choosing and his mercy
decisions.reason: The sentence has no subject. From verses 11-15 it is God's choice to show mercy: it does not come from a person's will or effort.

decisions.choice: running: effort, as of a runner in a race
decisions.reason: Paul often pictures effort as running (1 Corinthians 9:24-26, Galatians 2:2, Philippians 2:16).

decisions.choice: what a person wants; how hard a person strives (B); how hard they try (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "willing" and "running" stand for.

decisions.choice: God's choice
decisions.reason: Readable supplies the subject, as the meaning decision explains it.

source.text: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ τῷ Φαραὼ ὅτι Εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ἐξήγειρά σε ὅπως ἐνδείξωμαι ἐν σοὶ τὴν δύναμίν μου, καὶ ὅπως διαγγελῇ τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ.

records.literal_gloss: Says for the Scripture to the Pharaoh that: For this very [thing] I raised up you, so that I might show in you the power of me, and so that might be proclaimed the name of me in all the earth.

en.L: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh, "For this very [purpose] I raised you up, so that I might show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power in you, and so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name might be proclaimed in all the earth."
en.B: For Scripture says to Pharaoh, "This is the very reason I raised you up: to display {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power in you, and so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name would be made known through the whole earth."
en.R: In Scripture God says to Pharaoh, "This is the very reason I put you where you are: to show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power by what I do to you, so that people all over the earth will hear about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: Porque dice la Escritura a Faraón: «Para esto mismo te levanté, para mostrar en ti {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} poder, y para que {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre sea anunciado en toda la tierra».
es.B: Porque la Escritura le dice a Faraón: «Te levanté precisamente para esto: para mostrar en ti {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} poder, y para que {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre se dé a conocer por toda la tierra».
es.R: En la Escritura, Dios le dice a Faraón: «Te puse donde estás precisamente para esto: para mostrar {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} poder por lo que hago contigo, y para que la gente de toda la tierra oiga hablar de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».

sw.L: Kwa maana Maandiko yanamwambia Farao kwamba: "Kwa ajili ya jambo hili hasa nilikuinua, ili nionyeshe ndani yako nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, na ili jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} litangazwe katika dunia yote."
sw.B: Kwa maana Maandiko yanamwambia Farao, "Hii ndiyo sababu hasa nilikuinua: ili nionyeshe nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} kupitia wewe, na ili jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} lijulikane katika dunia nzima."
sw.R: Katika Maandiko Mungu anamwambia Farao, "Hii ndiyo sababu hasa nilikuweka mahali ulipo: ili nionyeshe nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} kwa yale ninayokutendea, na ili watu duniani kote wasikie habari {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}."

decisions.choice: Exodus 9:16
decisions.reason: God says this to Pharaoh through Moses during the plagues, before the hail. Paul's wording is close to the Greek Old Testament, with "raised you up" where it has "kept you".

decisions.choice: raised you up: brought you onto the scene
decisions.reason: ἐξεγείρω can mean to raise up or bring forward. In Exodus 9:16 the Hebrew means "I have let you stand", that is, kept you alive and in power. Paul's word puts the stress on God having brought Pharaoh into his place in history.

decisions.choice: Scripture says: God speaks in Scripture
decisions.reason: In Exodus God speaks these words; Paul says "the Scripture says", as he does in Galatians 3:8.

decisions.choice: my name: God himself, as he makes himself known
decisions.reason: God's name stands for who he is and his fame; the exodus made the God of Israel known among the nations (Exodus 15:14-16, Joshua 2:9-11).

decisions.choice: I put you where you are; will hear about me
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "raised you up" and "my name might be proclaimed" mean, following the meaning decisions.

decisions.choice: God says
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the speaker in Scripture.

source.text: ἄρα οὖν ὃν θέλει ἐλεεῖ, ὃν δὲ θέλει σκληρύνει.

records.literal_gloss: So then whom he wills he has mercy on, and whom he wills he hardens.

en.L: So then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has mercy on whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wills, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hardens whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wills.
en.B: So then God has mercy on whomever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hardens whomever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses.
en.R: So God shows mercy to anyone {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes stubborn anyone {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses.

es.L: Así pues, de quien quiere tiene misericordia, y a quien quiere endurece.
es.B: Así que Dios tiene misericordia de quien quiere, y endurece a quien quiere.
es.R: Así que Dios muestra misericordia a quien elige, y vuelve terco a quien elige.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo basi, anamrehemu yeyote anayetaka, na anamfanya kuwa mgumu yeyote anayetaka.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo Mungu anamrehemu yeyote anayemchagua, na anaufanya mgumu moyo wa yeyote anayemchagua.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Mungu anamwonyesha rehema yeyote anayemchagua, na anamfanya mkaidi yeyote anayemchagua.

decisions.choice: hardens: makes stubborn, unwilling to listen
alternatives: to make someone sinful who was not
decisions.reason: σκληρύνω is to make hard, and so to make a person stubborn against God. In Exodus God says he will harden Pharaoh's heart (4:21, 7:3), and Pharaoh also hardens his own heart (8:15, 8:32). Paul's conclusion draws on both verses 15 and 17.

decisions.choice: God is free in mercy and in hardening
decisions.reason: Paul states the conclusion of verses 15-17 without softening it. The objection in verse 19 shows that he means God's free decision; in 11:7-11 and 11:25-32 he says that Israel's hardening is partial and is not God's last word.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the subject.

decisions.choice: makes stubborn
decisions.reason: Readable says what "hardens" means here.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject pronoun inside the verb ("quiere", "elige"), so there is no free pronoun to capitalise, unlike the English "he".

decisions.choice: anaufanya mgumu moyo wa
decisions.reason: Said of a person, "kumfanya mtu mgumu" can mean making someone tough. Balanced names the heart, as Exodus does of Pharaoh, so the sense "unwilling to listen" is plain; Literal keeps the bare verb and Readable says "mkaidi" (stubborn).

source.text: Ἐρεῖς μοι οὖν· Τί οὖν ἔτι μέμφεται;

records.literal_gloss: You will say to me then: Why then still does he find fault?

en.L: You will say to me then, "Why then does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} still find fault?"
en.B: So you will say to me, "Why does God still find fault, then?"
en.R: Someone will say to me, "If that is true, why does God still blame people?"

es.L: Me dirás, pues: «¿Por qué, entonces, todavía culpa [a nadie]?»
es.B: Entonces me dirás: «¿Por qué Dios todavía culpa a la gente?»
es.R: Alguien me dirá: «Si eso es cierto, ¿por qué todavía culpa Dios a las personas?»

sw.L: Basi utaniambia, "Kwa nini basi bado anaona kosa?"
sw.B: Basi utaniambia, "Kwa nini basi Mungu bado anawalaumu watu?"
sw.R: Mtu fulani ataniambia, "Ikiwa ndivyo, kwa nini Mungu bado anawalaumu watu?"

decisions.choice: an imagined objector
decisions.reason: Paul answers an objection in the voice of an imagined speaker, as he does in 2:1-5, 3:1-8 and 11:19. The objection follows from verse 18.

decisions.choice: find fault: blame, hold people guilty
decisions.reason: μέμφομαι is to find fault with someone and hold them to blame.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the one who blames.

source.text: τῷ γὰρ βουλήματι αὐτοῦ τίς ἀνθέστηκεν;

records.literal_gloss: For the will of him who has resisted?

en.L: For who has resisted {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will?
en.B: For who can stand against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will?
en.R: After all, who can go against what God has decided?

es.L: Porque ¿quién ha resistido a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voluntad?
es.B: Porque ¿quién puede oponerse a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voluntad?
es.R: Al fin y al cabo, ¿quién puede ir en contra de lo que Dios ha decidido?

sw.L: Kwa maana ni nani ameyapinga mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}?
sw.B: Kwa maana ni nani awezaye kusimama dhidi ya mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}?
sw.R: Kwani, ni nani anayeweza kwenda kinyume na kile Mungu alichoamua?

decisions.choice: a rhetorical question: no one has ever resisted
decisions.reason: The perfect tense ἀνθέστηκεν means "who has taken a stand against". The objector means that no one can, so people cannot be blamed.

decisions.choice: his will: his settled purpose
decisions.reason: βούλημα is an intention or decision, here what God has decided to do.

decisions.choice: what God has decided
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says what "his will" means here.

source.text: ὦ ἄνθρωπε, μενοῦνγε σὺ τίς εἶ ὁ ἀνταποκρινόμενος τῷ θεῷ;

records.literal_gloss: O man, rather you who are, the [one] answering back to the God?

en.L: O {{gender:human|man}}, rather, who are you, the [one] who answers back to God?
en.B: But who are you, a mere human being, to answer back to God?
en.R: But you are only a human being. Who are you to argue with God?

es.L: ¡Oh {{gender:ser humano|hombre}}! Más bien, ¿quién eres tú, el que replica a Dios?
es.B: Pero ¿quién eres tú, un simple ser humano, para replicar a Dios?
es.R: Pero tú eres solo un ser humano. ¿Quién eres tú para discutir con Dios?

sw.L: Ewe mwanadamu, badala yake, wewe ni nani, wewe unayemrudishia Mungu majibu?
sw.B: Lakini wewe, uliye mwanadamu tu, ni nani hata ujibizane na Mungu?
sw.R: Lakini wewe ni mwanadamu tu. Wewe ni nani hata ubishane na Mungu?

decisions.choice: O man: a human being, in contrast to God
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπος here is a human being of either sex; the point is the difference between creature and Creator.

decisions.choice: rather: correcting the objector

decisions.choice: answering back: disputing with God

en.L: Will the thing formed say to the [one] who formed [it], "Why did you make me like this?"
en.B: Will what was shaped say to the one who shaped it, "Why did you make me this way?"
en.R: A clay pot does not say to the one who made it, "Why did you make me like this?"

es.B: ¿Le dirá la obra moldeada a quien la moldeó: «¿Por qué me hiciste de esta manera?»?

decisions.choice: Isaiah 29:16 and 45:9
decisions.reason: Isaiah twice pictures a pot speaking back to the potter who made it, to show how foolish it is for people to question their Maker. Paul uses the wording of Isaiah 29:16 in its Greek form.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: The question begins with μὴ: the thing made has no ground to complain to its maker.

decisions.choice: a clay pot
decisions.reason: Readable names the thing formed from the picture in verse 21, and turns the question into a statement, the answer it expects.

decisions.choice: kilichofinyangwa / aliyekifinyanga
decisions.reason: The Greek words are used of shaping clay, and verse 21 turns to the potter. "Kufinyanga" is the potter's verb and keeps that picture; "kuumba" (to create) would lose it. Balanced uses the plainer "kutengeneza" (to make).

source.text: ἢ οὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν ὁ κεραμεὺς τοῦ πηλοῦ ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ φυράματος ποιῆσαι ὃ μὲν εἰς τιμὴν σκεῦος ὃ δὲ εἰς ἀτιμίαν;

records.literal_gloss: Or not has authority the potter over the clay out of the same lump to make one for honor vessel, and one for dishonor?

en.L: Or does the potter not have authority over the clay, to make from the same lump one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?
en.B: Has the potter no right over the clay? From one and the same lump he may make one pot for honored use and another for common use.
en.R: A potter has the right to do what he wants with his clay. From the same lump he can make one pot for special use and another for everyday use.

es.L: ¿O no tiene el alfarero autoridad sobre el barro, para hacer de la misma masa una vasija para honra y otra para deshonra?
es.B: ¿No tiene el alfarero derecho sobre el barro? De una misma masa puede hacer una vasija para un uso honroso y otra para un uso común.
es.R: El alfarero tiene derecho a hacer lo que quiera con su barro. De la misma masa puede hacer una olla para ocasiones importantes y otra para el uso de todos los días.

sw.L: Au je, mfinyanzi hana mamlaka juu ya udongo, ili kutoka katika bonge lilelile afanye chombo kimoja kwa ajili ya heshima, na kingine kwa ajili ya kukosa heshima?

sw.R: Mfinyanzi ana mamlaka ya kufanya anavyotaka na udongo wake. Kutoka katika bonge lilelile anaweza kutengeneza chungu kimoja kwa ajili ya shughuli maalum na kingine kwa matumizi ya kila siku.

decisions.choice: the potter and the clay in Jeremiah 18:1-6
decisions.reason: At the potter's house God showed Jeremiah that, like clay in the potter's hand, Israel is in God's hand to shape (Jeremiah 18:6). Isaiah uses the same picture (29:16, 45:9, 64:8).

decisions.choice: honor and dishonor: honored use and common use
decisions.reason: The pots differ in use, not in quality: one for special occasions, one for ordinary or menial use, as in 2 Timothy 2:20.

decisions.choice: authority: the right to decide
decisions.reason: ἐξουσία is the right or authority to act; the potter has every right over his clay.

decisions.choice: a question followed by a statement (B); two statements (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced splits the long question; Readable states the answer the question expects (yes).

decisions.choice: mamlaka
decisions.reason: Everyday Swahili says "haki" for a right, but in Romans "haki" is the settled word for righteousness. "Mamlaka" (authority, the right to decide) keeps the two apart, as in John 1:12.

records.literal_gloss: But if wanting the God to show the wrath and to make known the power of him bore in much patience vessels of wrath having been prepared for destruction, \v 23 and so that he might make known the riches of the glory of him upon vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory, \v 24 whom also he called, us, not only from Jews but also from Gentiles, \v 25 as also in the Hosea he says: I will call the not people of me people of me, and the not having been loved having been loved;

en.L: But [what] if God, wanting to show the wrath and to make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power known, bore with much patience vessels of wrath prepared for destruction, \v 23 and [did so] in order to make known the riches of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory upon vessels of mercy, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} prepared beforehand for glory, \v 24 [even] us, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also called, not only from [the] Jews but also from [the] Gentiles? \v 25 As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also says in Hosea, "I will call [those who were] not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people '{{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people,' and her [who was] not loved 'loved.'"
en.B: What if God, wanting to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wrath and to make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power known, has borne with great patience the vessels of wrath, made ready for destruction? \v 23 What if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did this to make known the riches of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory to the vessels of mercy, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} prepared in advance for glory, \v 24 that is, to us, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has called not only from among the Jews but also from among the Gentiles? \v 25 As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says in Hosea, "Those who were not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people I will call '{{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people,' and her who was not loved I will call 'loved.'"
en.R: Suppose God wanted to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger and make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power known. Suppose {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been very patient with people who deserve {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger and are headed for destruction. \v 23 And suppose {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did this to show how great and rich {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory is to the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shown mercy to, people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} prepared long ago to share {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory. Who could complain about that? \v 24 We are those people. God has called us, and not only from among the Jews, but also from among people who are not Jews. \v 25 This is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says in the book of Hosea: "I will call those who were not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people '{{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.' I will call those who were not loved 'loved.'"

es.L: ¿Y qué si Dios, queriendo mostrar la ira y dar a conocer {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} poder, soportó con mucha paciencia [las] vasijas de ira preparadas para destrucción, \v 23 y [lo hizo] para dar a conocer las riquezas de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria sobre [las] vasijas de misericordia, que preparó de antemano para gloria, \v 24 [es decir], a nosotros, a quienes también llamó, no solo de entre [los] judíos sino también de entre [los] gentiles? \v 25 Como también dice en Oseas: «Llamaré “{{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo” al que no [era] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, y “amada” a la [que] no [era] amada».
es.B: ¿Y qué si Dios, queriendo mostrar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira y dar a conocer {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} poder, ha soportado con gran paciencia las vasijas de ira, dispuestas para la destrucción? \v 23 ¿Y qué si lo hizo para dar a conocer las riquezas de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria a las vasijas de misericordia, que preparó de antemano para la gloria, \v 24 es decir, a nosotros, a quienes ha llamado no solo de entre los judíos, sino también de entre los gentiles? \v 25 Como dice en Oseas: «A los que no eran {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo los llamaré “{{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo”, y a la que no era amada la llamaré “amada”».
es.R: Supongamos que Dios quiso mostrar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira y dar a conocer {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} poder. Supongamos que ha tenido mucha paciencia con gente que merece {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira y que va camino de la destrucción. \v 23 Y supongamos que lo hizo para mostrar cuán grande y rica es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria a las personas a quienes ha mostrado misericordia, personas que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} preparó hace mucho tiempo para compartir {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria. ¿Quién podría quejarse de eso? \v 24 Nosotros somos esas personas. Dios nos ha llamado, y no solo de entre los judíos, sino también de entre los que no son judíos. \v 25 Esto es lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dice en el libro de Oseas: «Llamaré “{{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo” a los que no eran {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo. Llamaré “amados” a los que no eran amados».

sw.L: Lakini [itakuwaje] ikiwa Mungu, akitaka kuonyesha ghadhabu na kujulisha nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, alistahimili kwa uvumilivu mwingi vyombo vya ghadhabu vilivyoandaliwa kwa ajili ya uharibifu, \v 23 na [alifanya hivyo] ili ajulishe utajiri wa utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} juu ya vyombo vya rehema, ambavyo alivitayarisha tangu mwanzo kwa ajili ya utukufu, \v 24 [yaani] sisi, ambao pia alituita, si kutoka kwa Wayahudi tu bali pia kutoka kwa watu wa mataifa? \v 25 Kama asemavyo pia katika [kitabu cha] Hosea: "Wale ambao hawakuwa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} nitawaita 'watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}},' na yule ambaye hakupendwa [nitamwita] 'mpendwa.'"
sw.B: Je, ikiwa Mungu, akitaka kuonyesha ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kujulisha nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, amevistahimili kwa uvumilivu mkubwa vyombo vya ghadhabu, vilivyoandaliwa kwa ajili ya uharibifu? \v 23 Je, ikiwa alifanya hivyo ili kujulisha utajiri wa utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa vyombo vya rehema, alivyoviandaa tangu mwanzo kwa ajili ya utukufu, \v 24 yaani sisi, ambao ametuita si kutoka miongoni mwa Wayahudi tu, bali pia kutoka miongoni mwa watu wa mataifa? \v 25 Kama asemavyo katika Hosea, "Wale ambao hawakuwa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} nitawaita 'watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}},' na yule ambaye hakupendwa nitamwita 'mpendwa.'"
sw.R: Tuseme Mungu alitaka kuonyesha ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kujulisha nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Tuseme amekuwa mvumilivu sana kwa watu wanaostahili ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na wanaoelekea kwenye uharibifu. \v 23 Na tuseme alifanya hivyo ili kuonyesha jinsi utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ulivyo mkuu na wenye utajiri mwingi kwa watu aliowaonyesha rehema, watu aliowaandaa tangu zamani ili washiriki utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Ni nani angeweza kulalamika juu ya hilo? \v 24 Sisi ndio watu hao. Mungu ametuita, na si kutoka miongoni mwa Wayahudi tu, bali pia kutoka miongoni mwa watu wasio Wayahudi. \v 25 Hivi ndivyo anavyosema katika kitabu cha Hosea: "Wale ambao hawakuwa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} nitawaita 'watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.' Wale ambao hawakupendwa nitawaita 'wapendwa.'"

decisions.choice: an "if" with no "then": the conclusion is left for the reader
alternatives: a statement of what God has done
decisions.reason: Paul begins "but if God ..." and never finishes the sentence: after the Hosea quotation he moves on. The unstated conclusion is most likely "who are you to object?" (verse 20), or "is God not free to do this?" In context the sentence works as a question: "what if God ...?"

decisions.choice: wanting: either "although he wanted" or "because he wanted"
decisions.reason: The participle θέλων can mean that God bore with them patiently although he wanted to show his wrath (holding it back, as in 2:4), or because he wanted to show it more fully in the end. The first fits Paul's stress on God's patience and on his purpose of mercy in verse 23 and in 11:22-32, but the participle itself allows both.

decisions.choice: prepared for destruction: Paul does not say by whom
decisions.reason: Of the vessels of mercy Paul says "which he prepared beforehand" (verse 23), with God as subject. Of the vessels of wrath he uses a passive or middle perfect, κατηρτισμένα, "made ready", without naming who made them ready. Some read it as God's doing, others as their own (compare 2:4-5, where impenitence stores up wrath).

decisions.choice: vessels: pots, meaning people
decisions.reason: σκεῦος continues the potter's picture from verse 21: people are the pots, made for wrath or for mercy.

decisions.choice: wrath: God's judgment against sin
decisions.reason: As in 1:18 and 2:5, ὀργή is God's settled opposition to evil and his judgment on it, not a fit of temper.

decisions.choice: Hosea 2:23 (2:25 in the Hebrew)
decisions.reason: Hosea's children were named "Not my people" and "Not pitied" as a sign of God's judgment on Israel, and God promised to reverse the names (Hosea 1:6-9, 2:23). Paul quotes freely, with "I will call" and "loved" where the Greek Old Testament has "I will say" and "pitied". He applies to Gentiles a promise first spoken to Israel: God makes his people of those who were not.

decisions.choice: Suppose ... Who could complain about that?
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the unfinished sentence into short "suppose" sentences and states the question the meaning decision takes to be implied.

decisions.choice: anger
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for wrath.

decisions.choice: vessels
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "vessels", which ties back to the potter in verse 21; Readable says "people", the meaning of the picture.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says "people who are not Jews" for "Gentiles", as Romans 1 does.

decisions.choice: ira
decisions.reason: As in 1:18, Spanish "ira" is an everyday word, so Readable keeps the key term where the English Readable says "anger".

decisions.choice: ghadhabu
decisions.reason: As in 1:18, "ghadhabu" is the settled word for God's wrath and is well known, so Readable keeps it; "hasira" is ordinary human anger.

en.B: "And in the place where they were told, 'You are not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people,' that is where they will be called {{gender:children|sons}} of the living God."

sw.B: "Na palepale walipoambiwa, 'Ninyi si watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}},' ndipo watakapoitwa wana wa Mungu aliye hai."
sw.R: "Mahali palepale ambapo waliambiwa, 'Ninyi si watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}},' wataitwa wana wa Mungu aliye hai."

decisions.choice: Hosea 1:10 (2:1 in the Hebrew)
decisions.reason: Paul joins a second promise from Hosea to the first, word for word as in the Greek Old Testament: the people once disowned will be called children of the living God. In Hosea the place is the land of Israel; Paul applies the promise to Gentiles wherever God calls them (verse 24).

decisions.choice: sons: children of God, women and men
decisions.reason: The phrase speaks of the people as God's family and heirs, as in 8:14-17, where sons and children are used together. It includes women and men alike.

decisions.choice: the living God: the true God, in contrast to idols
decisions.reason: The title marks the God of Israel as the one who lives and gives life, unlike the idols Hosea condemns (Hosea 4:12-13; compare 1 Thessalonians 1:9).

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Ustedes no son|Vosotros no sois}}
decisions.reason: The first plural "you" in this chapter, inside the Hosea quotation. As everywhere in Romans, it takes the reader setting: ustedes (the default) or vosotros.

decisions.choice: hijos, no setting
decisions.reason: As with "hermanos" in verse 3, Spanish "hijos" already includes daughters, so there is no gender span here or in verse 27.

decisions.choice: wana, no setting
alternatives: wana wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: "Wana" (children, sons) already includes daughters, so Swahili needs no gender span here or in verse 27.

records.literal_gloss: Isaiah and cries out on behalf of the Israel: If be the number of the sons of Israel as the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved;

en.L: And Isaiah cries out concerning Israel, "If the number of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel be as the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved;"
en.B: And Isaiah cries out about Israel: "Though the people of Israel are as many as the grains of sand by the sea, the remnant will be saved."
en.R: Isaiah also called out this message about Israel: "The people of Israel may be as many as the grains of sand on the seashore. But it is the remnant, the ones who are left, who will be saved."

es.L: E Isaías clama acerca de Israel: «Aunque el número de los hijos de Israel sea como la arena del mar, el remanente será salvo».
es.B: E Isaías proclama acerca de Israel: «Aunque los israelitas sean tan numerosos como los granos de arena del mar, el remanente se salvará».

sw.L: Na Isaya analia kuhusu Israeli: "Hata kama hesabu ya wana wa Israeli itakuwa kama mchanga wa bahari, mabaki yataokolewa;"
sw.B: Na Isaya anatangaza kwa sauti kuhusu Israeli: "Ingawa watu wa Israeli ni wengi kama chembe za mchanga wa pwani, mabaki yataokolewa."

decisions.choice: Isaiah 10:22, with Hosea 1:10
decisions.reason: Isaiah 10:22-23 says that though Israel is as many as the sand of the sea, only a remnant will return, for destruction has been decreed. Paul begins with the words of Hosea 1:10, "the number of the sons of Israel", which he has just quoted from (verse 26). The Hebrew of Isaiah has "return", which the Greek Old Testament gives as "will be saved".

decisions.choice: the remnant: both warning and hope
alternatives: only a remnant will be saved (warning only)
a remnant will surely be saved (hope only)
decisions.reason: The words warn that not all Israel, but a remnant, will be saved (verse 6). They also promise that a remnant will surely be saved, as Paul says in 11:5. Paul may mean both; the Greek says "the remnant will be saved", with no word for "only".

decisions.choice: cries out: proclaims aloud, as a prophet
decisions.reason: κράζω is to shout or cry out; here it is a prophet's urgent message.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the people of Israel" for "the sons of Israel", which means all the Israelites.

decisions.choice: the ones who are left
decisions.reason: Readable explains "remnant".

decisions.choice: mabaki
decisions.reason: "Mabaki" (what is left) matches Romans 11:5, where Paul returns to the remnant in the same argument. "Masalia", a remnant that survives, is the alternative; a reviewer may prefer it, since "mabaki" is also used of leftovers such as food.

source.text: λόγον γὰρ συντελῶν καὶ συντέμνων ποιήσει κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Word for completing and cutting short will do Lord upon the earth.

en.L: "For [the] Lord will carry out [the] word upon the earth, completing [it] and cutting [it] short."
en.B: "For on the earth the Lord will carry out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sentence, fully and without delay."
en.R: "The Lord will do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do on the earth. He will do it completely and quickly."

es.L: «Porque [el] Señor llevará a cabo [la] palabra sobre la tierra, consumándola y abreviándola».
es.B: «Porque el Señor ejecutará {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sentencia sobre la tierra, por completo y sin demora».
es.R: «El Señor hará en la tierra lo que ha dicho que hará. Lo hará por completo y rápidamente».
